name: Sprocket
text: Build a self-review loop where every prompt update triggers an automated review of the same task set we used to validate the last version. This keeps quality high without manual checks. The trade-off is higher compute cost for every tweak, but it prevents silent regressions that hurt user trust.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just higher compute cost—it’s that testing 500 tasks after every tweak guarantees we’ll hit false positives or edge cases that waste time debugging noise instead of shipping. A better alternative: run the review loop only on *meaningful* prompt changes (e.g., structural shifts, not word swaps), with a human sanity-check gate before triggering tests. That settles it: prove the change alters core logic or intent, not just phrasing.

name: Sprocket
text:
DO: Run the new prompt against a fresh, diverse batch of 500 tasks *before* deploying any change. The trade-off is slower iteration speed, but it catches silent regressions that erode user trust and avoids the noise of false positives from partial testing. This keeps quality high without relying on manual checks or risky heuristics like "meaningful changes."

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower iteration—it’s that a fresh 500-task batch might miss the *specific* edge cases your last tweak broke, since diversity doesn’t guarantee coverage. A better alternative: run the review loop on *both* the old and new prompts against the *same* 500 tasks, then compare side-by-side for regressions. That settles the argument by isolating changes’ impact without wasting compute on unrelated noise.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower iteration—it’s that running 500 tasks *before* every change turns the review loop into a bottleneck that delays fixes for real user pain. A better alternative: gate meaningful changes with a lightweight pre-check (e.g., 50 diverse tasks) and reserve the full 500-task suite for *post-change* validation only when the pre-check flags anomalies. Settle it by measuring: track how often the full suite catches regressions that the pre-check misses, and adjust the threshold until the trade-off favors speed *and* safety.
